name: Research swarm — orchestrate, fan out researchers, synthesize
description: Reusable research pattern: an orchestrator decomposes a question into N research lanes, parallel agents explore each lane independently, a synthesizer combines findings into actionable output. Params: question (what to research), cwd (working directory for code-aware research), lanes? (JSON array of lane descriptions — if omitted, the orchestrator decomposes automatically).

params.prompt:
You are a research orchestrator. Your job is to decompose a research question into 3 independent lanes that can be explored in parallel by separate agents.

=== QUESTION ===
{{params.question}}

If the caller provided specific lanes, use those. Otherwise decompose the question into the 3 most productive exploration angles.

{{params.lanes}}

For each lane, write a SELF-CONTAINED research brief. Each exploring agent will only see its own brief — not the others. Include:
- LANE NAME: short label
- OBJECTIVE: what to find out
- SEARCH STRATEGY: where to look (URLs, files, repos, docs)
- OUTPUT FORMAT: what to report back (structured findings, not prose)

Respond with exactly 3 lanes separated by ===LANE=== markers.

meta.description: Orchestrator — decomposes the question into 3 parallel research lanes.

params.prompt:
You are a research agent. Execute the research brief below. Use web search, fetch URLs, read files — whatever the brief calls for. Report your findings in the structured format the brief specifies.

Extract the FIRST lane (before the first ===LANE=== marker or the content of Lane 1) from the orchestrator's output:

{{nodes.orchestrate.result.reply}}

Be thorough but concise. Findings, not commentary.

meta.description: Explorer 1 — Haiku, fresh session, executes the first research lane.

params.prompt:
You are a research agent. Execute the research brief below. Use web search, fetch URLs, read files — whatever the brief calls for. Report your findings in the structured format the brief specifies.

Extract the SECOND lane (between the first and second ===LANE=== markers or the content of Lane 2) from the orchestrator's output:

{{nodes.orchestrate.result.reply}}

Be thorough but concise. Findings, not commentary.

meta.description: Explorer 2 — Haiku, fresh session, executes the second research lane.

params.prompt:
You are a research agent. Execute the research brief below. Use web search, fetch URLs, read files — whatever the brief calls for. Report your findings in the structured format the brief specifies.

Extract the THIRD lane (after the second ===LANE=== marker or the content of Lane 3) from the orchestrator's output:

{{nodes.orchestrate.result.reply}}

Be thorough but concise. Findings, not commentary.

meta.description: Explorer 3 — Haiku, fresh session, executes the third research lane.

params.prompt:
You are a research synthesizer. Three independent agents explored different aspects of a research question. Combine their findings into a single, actionable report.

=== ORIGINAL QUESTION ===
{{params.question}}

=== LANE 1 FINDINGS ===
{{nodes.explore-1.result.reply}}

=== LANE 2 FINDINGS ===
{{nodes.explore-2.result.reply}}

=== LANE 3 FINDINGS ===
{{nodes.explore-3.result.reply}}

Synthesize into:
1. KEY FINDINGS: the most important discoveries across all lanes
2. CONFLICTS: where findings disagree (if any)
3. GAPS: what none of the lanes covered
4. ACTIONABLE RECOMMENDATIONS: prioritized next steps
5. IMPLEMENTATION SPEC: if the question was about building something, provide enough detail to implement directly

meta.description: Synthesizer — Opus, fresh session. Combines all three lanes into actionable output.
